subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Goal-line technology in football is an example of technology used to:
options: Give officials accurate decisions on whether the ball crossed the line
questions.explain: Goal-line technology helps officials decide accurately whether the whole ball has crossed the goal line.

questions.q: Verbal guidance is best described as:
options: Telling or explaining to a performer how to do something
questions.explain: Verbal guidance involves explaining or describing a skill using spoken words.

questions.q: Manual guidance involves:
options: Physically supporting or moving the performer's body
Telling the performer what to do
questions.explain: Manual guidance is physically supporting or moving a performer through the correct movement.

questions.q: Hooliganism among spectators is an example of:
questions.explain: Hooliganism is violent or disorderly spectator behaviour, a form of deviance associated with sport.

questions.q: The vertical jump test (Sargent jump) is used to measure which component of fitness?
questions.explain: The vertical jump test measures explosive leg power.

questions.q: A 50-year-old's estimated maximum heart rate using the standard formula is:
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 50 = 170 bpm.

questions.q: A performer who is outgoing, sociable and enjoys high-arousal situations is likely a(n):
questions.explain: Extroverts are outgoing and sociable and tend to perform well in high-arousal, dynamic activities.

questions.q: According to the inverted-U theory, if arousal becomes too high, performance will:
questions.explain: Once arousal passes the optimal point, performance declines because the athlete becomes over-aroused.

questions.q: Which energy system provides energy for an explosive movement lasting up to about 10 seconds, such as a sprint start?
questions.explain: The ATP-PC system provides immediate energy without oxygen for short, maximal efforts of up to around 10 seconds.

questions.q: In the basic information-processing model, the correct order is:
questions.explain: Information processing follows input (stimulus), decision-making, output (response) and then feedback.

questions.q: What is the maximum heart rate of a 15-year-old using the standard formula?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 15 = 205 bpm.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cool-down after exercise?
options: To gradually lower heart rate and remove waste products
questions.explain: A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate and helps remove lactic acid, reducing stiffness.

questions.q: A coach's written opinion on a player's effort is an example of:
questions.explain: Qualitative data is descriptive and based on opinions, judgements or observations.

questions.q: Cardiac output is calculated by multiplying:
questions.explain: Cardiac output equals stroke volume multiplied by heart rate, giving the blood pumped per minute.

questions.q: A negative effect of the media's influence on sport is:
options: Loss of atmosphere when fewer fans attend live events
questions.explain: Demand for televised sport can reduce live attendance and focus coverage on a few popular sports.

questions.q: The aerobic training zone is generally regarded as roughly what percentage of maximum heart rate?
questions.explain: The aerobic training zone lies at about 60-80% of maximum heart rate, where the body works mainly using oxygen.

questions.q: Circuit training is best described as:
options: A series of exercise stations completed in turn
Running at a constant steady pace for a long time
Lifting one heavy weight to failure
questions.explain: Circuit training involves moving between a series of stations, each with a different exercise.

questions.q: A pie chart is most useful for showing:
options: Change in heart rate over time
Proportions of a whole, such as percentage of training time per method
questions.explain: Pie charts show how a whole is divided into proportions or percentages.

questions.q: A basic (simple) skill is one that:
options: Requires complex coordination of many subroutines
Can only be performed by elite athletes
questions.explain: Basic skills require little concentration or decision-making, such as running or a chest pass.

questions.q: What does the 'A' in SMART goal setting stand for?
questions.explain: In SMART targets the A stands for Achievable, so the goal is within the performer's reach.

questions.q: Anxiety in sport can be described as:
options: A negative emotional state linked to worry or nervousness
questions.explain: Anxiety is a negative emotional state involving feelings of worry, nervousness and apprehension.

questions.q: Which performer is most likely to benefit from an endomorph somatotype?
questions.explain: Endomorphs carry more body mass, which can be an advantage in sports such as sumo wrestling.
